records.name: Hike + Heal
records.summary: A women's hiking and wellness group that runs healing hikes, weekday happy hour hikes, field trips and retreats for women of all fitness levels.
records.what_you_do: Join a healing hike or happy hour hike, a wellness event, a field trip or a retreat. Events are posted on its calendar, and some are hosted with partner groups.

schedule.text: Healing hikes, weekday happy hour hikes, wellness events and retreats, posted on its calendar as they are planned.

locations.label: Events in the Philadelphia suburbs and Wilmington, DE, per its calendar

cost.text: The yearly Hive membership is $350, and enrollment is closed for now with a waitlist. Event prices are not shown on the website, so check each listing.

access.notes: The site calls its wellness events accessible and body inclusive, but gives no details on trails, mobility help or getting there.

first_step.how: Sign up for the next hike through the 'join our next hike' link on the website, which goes to its Luma calendar.
first_step.basis: The site says women of all fitness levels and no experience are welcome and links straight to sign-up, but it does not say whether non-members can join events.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes its events as welcoming and focused on meeting other women and spending time outdoors. Hike length, difficulty and price are not on the website, so read the event page before you go.
first_visit_tips: Wear sneakers, which the site lists as what to bring.
Check the event page for the meeting place and price before you sign up.

records.notes: The Hive enrollment window runs each year from November 28 to February 28, and the site gives no year for the current window. The Luma calendar lists October events (a harvest hayride and bonfire in Delaware marked sold out, and a family photo hike) without a year. Two co-hosts named on the photo hike are on Luma, not the group's own site, so they are not listed as leads.

records.name: Historic Strawberry Mansion Orchard
records.summary: The orchard and kitchen garden at Historic Strawberry Mansion in East Fairmount Park, planted with the Philadelphia Orchard Project. Community members are welcome to pick fruit from the orchard trees, and the mansion hosts workshops on using the fruit.
records.what_you_do: Pick fruit from the orchard trees as a community member (call first, since the site gives no picking rules), take a walk-in mansion tour, or email the mansion about volunteering in the gardens and orchard.

schedule.text: Walk-in mansion tours run Thursday through Sunday, 10 am to 3 pm, with guided tours starting on the hour. The site gives no separate hours for the grounds.

cost.text: Walk-in tours cost $8 for general admission, $5 for students, youth and seniors, and are free for veterans and active-duty military. Groups of 10 or more pay $5 each with advance registration.

access.notes: The first floor is ADA compliant. Upper floors are reached only by stairs, and the site offers virtual tours for visitors who cannot climb them. Nearest SEPTA stop named on the site: the Route 32 bus at 33rd Street near Dauphin Street, a short walk away.

first_step.how: Come to a walk-in tour Thursday to Sunday, 10 am to 3 pm, or call 215-228-8364 to ask about picking fruit or volunteering in the gardens.
first_step.basis: Tours are walk-in and open to the public, and volunteer questions go to an email address, with no online form described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tours are guided and start on the hour, taking you through rooms of antiques, fine art and collectibles from the 18th and 19th centuries. The site does not say how long a tour takes. Volunteers work in the gardens and orchard, and the site describes no training or set hours.
first_visit_tips: Bring cash or a check, since the mansion does not take cards.
Ask about virtual tour options before you come if you cannot use the stairs.
Parking is free and off-street for up to 50 vehicles.
Take SEPTA bus Route 32 to the stop on 33rd Street near Dauphin Street.

records.notes: Volunteer questions go to the mansion by email. The get-involved page also lists info@phillyorchards.org for the Philadelphia Orchard Project. The site does not say when community members may pick fruit or what the rules are. The art exhibition runs Thursday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm, until November 8, 2026, and the events page gives no admission price for it.

records.name: Holmesburg United Methodist Church
records.summary: A United Methodist church on Frankford Avenue with Sunday worship at 10:30 am, a Tuesday food pantry open to the community, and a community program called Ann's Attic.
records.what_you_do: Attend Sunday worship, use the Tuesday food pantry, or shop at Ann's Attic, the church's thrift shop, during its set hours. Teen Bible meets on Tuesday evenings.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am. Food pantry on Tuesdays, 10 am to 2 pm. Ann's Attic on Mondays noon to 2 pm, Wednesdays 10 am to 2 pm, and the first and third Saturdays 10 am to 2 pm. Teen Bible on Tuesdays at 7 pm.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, or call 215-624-6900 or email holmesburgumc@gmail.com before a first visit.
first_step.basis: The site invites friends, family and neighbors to worship and gives a phone number, an email and a contact form, but it does not describe a welcome process.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:30 am at the church on Frankford Avenue. The site calls the congregation inclusive and welcoming, but it does not describe the service, how long it runs or what to wear. Calling ahead is the best way to learn what a first visit is like.
first_visit_tips: Call or email ahead to ask what the service is like.
The site does not list parking or transit, so ask when you call.

records.notes: The events and activities page lists no events, and the only year on the site is a 2023 copyright line, so the probably_active status rests on the working site alone. The about page describes a King's Kitchen meal service in the Fellowship Hall that feeds anyone in need, but it gives no days or hours, so it is not listed here. Accessibility, parking and transit are not described.

records.name: Holobiont Laboratory
records.summary: A community lab based at Karakung Reef in West Philadelphia that tests climate ideas with neighbors. Its projects include solar installs, a heat shelter with solar-powered sprinklers, and hands-on solar and papermaking sessions.
records.what_you_do: Come to the lab's public events, such as the off-grid solar session (date to be announced) or a zine launch party. Subscribe to its email updates to hear when new events are scheduled.

schedule.text: Events are added to the lab's events page as they are planned. No regular weekly or monthly meeting is listed.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the email updates through the link on holobiontlab.org, then come to the next open event, such as the off-grid solar workshop once its date is set.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly and an email sign-up is offered, but the site does not say how to register for an event or what one costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are one-off, hands-on sessions. The off-grid solar workshop covers the basics of how a small solar system works, and you build a small working system yourself. The site gives no cost or length for events, so ask through the contact page before you come.
first_visit_tips: Subscribe to the email list so you hear when the solar workshop date is set.
The solar workshop is at Karakung Reef, which the event page says is reachable on the 34 trolley.

records.notes: Mailing address is PO Box 23462, Philadelphia, PA 19143, per the contact page. The site publishes no email or phone. The events page lists the zine launch party for February 28, 2026 under Coming Up, so that label may be out of date. A Lab Notes entry mentions a May 6 papermaking workshop with no year. The about page says the lab began in June 2020.

records.name: Holy Angels Parish (Korean)
records.summary: A Korean-language Catholic parish on Old York Road with several Sunday Masses, and Masses on Tuesday and Thursday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in Korean. Confession is offered before and after Mass. Parish groups such as the choir, the library and a Friday evening Bible reflection meet, but the site does not explain how to sign up, so call the office.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7 am, 10 am, 11:30 am and 5 pm, all in Korean. Saturday vigil Mass at 8 pm. Tuesday and Thursday Mass at 8 pm.

first_step.how: Come to any Mass listed above, and call the parish office to confirm the times before your first visit.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the site lists an inquirers' class for people preparing to join, but it does not describe a welcome for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is said in Korean and is free to attend. The site does not describe a first visit or say whether any service is offered in English. Confession is offered before and after Mass, so you can go before or after the service.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-927-1662 to confirm the times, since the parish site does not mark am or pm and listings can change.
If you want to become Catholic, ask about the inquirers' class, which starts in September and meets each morning at 8:30 am. The site gives no year.

records.notes: The parish site is in Korean and its weekly bulletin is a PDF, so the Sunday am and pm times come from an archdiocese listing summarized by a search, not from the parish's own page. Confirm by phone before a first visit, since an older 2002 listing showed fewer Sunday Masses. Fax (215) 224-6615 is on the contact page. The site has only a web form, no email, and no office hours. Parking and accessibility are not published. The groups page lists 26 groups, including Sunday school, a choir, a library, Marriage Encounter and a youth group, with no sign-up details.

records.name: Holy Communion Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation downtown with Sunday worship, a food pantry on the second Wednesday of each month, and a 150th anniversary dinner planned for November 7, 2026.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, join the Monday Welcome Church Bible study at 11 am, or visit the food pantry on the second Wednesday of the month. Senior food boxes are handed out on the third Wednesday.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am. Food pantry (Food Cabinet) on the second Wednesday of the month, with distribution from 11 am to 1 pm according to the October 2026 calendar. Senior food boxes on the third Wednesday. Welcome Church Bible study on Mondays at 11 am.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, or contact Pastor Terri at info@lc-hc.org or 215-567-3668 to ask how to join the congregation.
first_step.basis: The site says the church is open to all, invites newcomers to join, and tells visitors to contact the pastor to learn how to become part of the congregation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship at 11 am includes Communion. The site says the service is live-streamed on Facebook and posted to YouTube, so you can watch first. It does not describe the service in more detail or say whether there is a welcome table.
first_visit_tips: Enter the Sanctuary from 2110 Chestnut Street; the church office door is at 2111 Sansom Street.
Parking and transit are not listed on the site, so call the office first.

records.notes: The pantry hours conflict: an older announcement says 11 am to 12:30 pm on the second Wednesday, while the October 2026 calendar lists distribution from 11 am to 1 pm. The record uses the calendar, so confirm before a visit. The announcement does not say who may come or whether to sign up. The calendar shows public events only and does not say whether any are members only.

records.name: Holy Cross Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish in Mount Airy with Sunday Masses, a Saturday evening Vigil Mass, and a parish school on East Mount Airy Avenue. A food pantry on East Mount Airy Avenue is also listed.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or call the parish office to ask about groups such as the Legion of Mary, Stewards of Our Earth, the greeters and ushers team, or the Ladies Guild. The parish's HOPE Food Pantry serves neighbors, but the site gives no hours.

schedule.text: Saturday Vigil Mass at 5 pm. Sunday Masses at 9 am (livestreamed), 11 am and 6 pm. Weekday Mass Tuesday to Friday at 8 am. Confession Saturdays 4 to 4:30 pm or by appointment.

access.notes: The site says the church is wheelchair accessible. It does not describe the entrance or whether there is an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to any Mass listed above, then register online or pick up a paper form at the parish office to join Holy Cross.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome and invites visitors to come and see, and it offers an online form and paper forms for joining the parish.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. The site does not describe what a first visit is like or how long Mass runs, but the 9 am Sunday Mass is livestreamed if you want to watch first. Ask the parish office how to join a group if you want to volunteer.
first_visit_tips: The parish office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm, at 154 E. Mt. Airy Ave.
Paper join forms are at the parish office, and the online form is linked from the site.

records.notes: The Flocknote posts announce Father Kevin Okafor's installation as pastor at the 10 am Mass on October 4, 2026. The church address is 140 E. Mt. Airy Ave. (per the directions page), and the parish office is at 154, so the tier 1 record's single address is split into two locations. The HOPE Food Pantry has no days or hours on the site. The religious education registration page gives no age range, schedule or cost. The Archdiocese day of service list from July 3, 2026 names a food pantry at 140 E. Mt. Airy Ave. with no hours.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Orchard Project
leads_only.note: Named on the Strawberry Mansion pages as the orchard partner. Checked 2026-10-08: a volunteer nonprofit that helps community groups plant and care for orchards, with volunteer work days across Philadelphia and a volunteer email list. Not turned into a record in this batch because it is the parent of the orchard above and needs its own pass; strong candidate for the next wave.

leads_only.name: Philabundance
leads_only.note: Named on the Holy Communion calendar as the source of the senior food boxes. Checked 2026-10-08: a nine county food bank with community programs for qualifying adults. Dropped as a record: it is a regional food bank rather than a neighborhood group, and its site gives no senior food box details.

notes: All seven groups deep-read: each group's own pages were fetched (5 to 6 per group), and the one WebSearch was used for Holy Angels' Sunday Mass times, which the Korean parish site does not mark am or pm. Those times come from an archdiocese listing summarized by search, not from a fetched page, so they are flagged in that record. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide. Status changes: Strawberry Mansion moved to active (October 2026 events on its own site). Holy Angels and Holy Cross stay active on dated 2026 posts. Holobiont Laboratory's newcomer rating moved from 3 to 2, because the site does not say how to register for its events. Hike + Heal's Hive membership ($350 a year) is closed to new members with a waitlist, and the site does not say whether non-members can attend events. Holy Cross's church address was corrected and wheelchair access is recorded as yes from its directions page. Holy Communion's food pantry hours conflict between two of its own pages (noted in its record). No blocked pages, bot checks or rate limits were hit. Leads checked: Philadelphia Orchard Project and Philabundance (see leads_only). Co-hosts named on Hike + Heal's Luma calendar are not on the group's own site and are not listed.
